dedupe_keys.name: polaris agent based freight model with passenger and freight market interactions

description: This model, described by Monique Stinson, Joshua Auld and Abolfazl Mohammadian of Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Chicago (Procedia Computer Science, 2020), is the first stage of an agent-based freight modelling system built inside POLARIS, Argonne's C++ Planning and Operations Language for Agent-based Regional Integrated Simulation, which already combines activity-based passenger demand with dynamic traffic assignment. Coverage: a global representation of agents on a detailed large-scale network, used to evaluate the transport and energy impacts of goods movement from urban to national scale. Features include a parcel location assignment algorithm for business establishments, estimation of establishment production and consumption, push-pull supply chains, multimodal path choice, logistics node choice, dynamic traffic assignment, and an e-commerce module for last-mile delivery energy use and congestion. Format and access: an open access conference paper. Licence and cost: the paper is free under CC BY-NC-ND; access to POLARIS itself follows Argonne's terms, which the paper does not state. Caveats: an initial implementation, so behaviour models were still being extended. It can simulate interacting passenger and freight traffic for congestion, energy and disruption scenarios. It relates to POLARIS and the CMAP tour-based freight model in the catalogue.
